_about: Boeing (Douglas), DC-9 Airplane Characteristics for Airport Planning (June 1984, Rev F 5/84; the copy on boeing.com's airport planning page, 2023), 2.2 General Airplane Dimensions, Model DC-9-32 (page index 14): side, plan and front views on one sheet, a 1-bit scan on graph paper (about 47 px a meter at scale 4). layers.py --mode image at scale 4 --unrotate --rotate 179.57, clip 72,310,530,424 (stored page points: the page is stored turned, and the scan is drawn 0.43 degrees off level). Pixels of that raster, line centres. The grid's lines run through the drawing: the nose tip sits on one (x 41-43), the cabin's crown runs along another (y 238-240) from the windshield to about x 260, and the belly crosses one under the nose (y 380) and under the tail (y 381). The main gear's wheel stands below the belly. The nacelle stands beside the fuselage, between crown and belly, so neither is hidden. Fin: the fillet leaves the crown at about x 1300; the leading edge runs up to the top fairing, whose top the 36.36 m dimension's extension line runs along (y 55); the fin's top is the fairing's top (as the MD-80's): fin.leading ends on it, fin.trailing runs up the trailing edge behind the tailplane to the fairing's pointed tail (1747, 83) and back along its top. The trailing edge rises from the crown at 1541; the rudder's hinge line (with its three hinge fairings) is fin.rudder. The tailplane is drawn across the fin's top (not traced here: the plan's and front view's). The nacelle: the JT8D's inlet at x 1118, the fan cowl's end at 1326.5 (cowlEnd), then the target thrust reverser and the nozzle's cone to its tip.
